flags.item: The three submitted identifiers are not 10-character ASINs
flags.detail: The identifiers in the submitted links are B04G1MEwY, B02NbDxp3 and B00hJ57DV. Each is 9 characters long. The official Creators API documentation shows ASIN examples of 10 characters (S06), and all three redirect targets use 10-character IDs (S14-S16). Typing amazon.com/dp/<each ID> returns 'Page Not Found' (S08-S10). No product name, brand, price, rating or commission can be tied to these identifiers. Confirmed by the GetItems reference (S06, chunk 1 of 3): an ASIN is a 10-character identifier.
flags.action: Provide the intended product page URL or 10-character ASIN for each product (the owner's input is needed; this session cannot infer it). Update 2026-11-14: the listing each link opens is now recorded (FLG-022); the request for owner confirmation of intent stands.

flags.item: Short links redirect to three different products, not confirmed as the submitted products
flags.detail: Each short link ended on a different amazon.com product page (S11-S13), and the mapping was the same on two fetches each. The final URLs carry the parameters lv=shuf and plpRedirect=mhFallback. The page titles identify two CHEFMAN air fryers and one Emeril Lagasse air fryer toaster oven (S14-S16). What these parameters mean is not documented in any official source reviewed, so they are recorded as observed only and never used as product data. The direct amazon.com/dp/B08DKYBTPH request returns a 'Continue shopping' interstitial (S16), so product 3's title is only readable through the short link (S23). Update 2026-11-14 (session 9fef7647): all three links were re-fetched with fresh redirect tokens and each resolved to the same listing as on 2026-11-13 (S30-S32). The 'not confirmed' wording now refers only to the owner's intent (which product was meant by the code), not to the stability of the mapping, which has been observed 4 times over 2 days (FLG-022, FLG-024).
flags.action: Open each submitted link in a normal browser and confirm where it lands. Confirm which product was intended.

flags.item: link.amazon links are not documented in the Associates policies reviewed and may be Redirecting Links
flags.detail: The Program Policies reviewed (S02) do not name link.amazon. The policies prohibit a link shortener that makes the Amazon destination unclear (PF-06, section 6(w)). They also disqualify purchases referred by a Redirecting Link, meaning a link that sends users through an intermediate site without a customer click (PF-07). The short links redirected automatically to amazon.com in the fetch tool (S11-S13). A third-party competitor claims link.amazon forwards to amzlinks.in (S17). That claim is not verified against any Amazon page.
flags.action: Test each link while logged in to an Associates account and record whether tracked clicks appear. Generate Special Links from Associates Central instead, if the owner wants to use them.

flags.item: Product name, brand, price, rating, review count, competitor count, best-seller rank and availability are unverified for all 3 products
flags.detail: The identifiers do not resolve (FLG-001), so no official product record exists to read these values from. The fetch tool returned only the page title and the URL for the redirect targets (S14-S16); prices and ratings were not in its text. These cells are left blank on purpose. Update 2026-11-14 (session 9fef7647): price, rating and review count are now shown as dated snapshots observed on Amazon's own search pages (S33-S35). They are volatile deal prices and their display on a live Associates site is restricted by Participation Requirements 2(b) and 6(t) (PF-04, PF-05) - see FLG-023. Competitor count, best-seller rank, availability, clicks and conversions remain unverified and blank.
flags.action: After FLG-001 is fixed, read the values from the Creators API (see FLG-006) or the live product page, then add them to data/products.json with a source ID.

flags.item: Commission rates are unverified; the official rate schedule is not accessible
flags.detail: The Commission Schedule link in the Program Policies (S03) redirected to an Amazon sign-in page on 2026-11-13. No rate was read, so no commission rate, commission-income estimate or payout figure is stated on this site.
flags.action: Sign in to Associates Central and export the rate card for the product category; send the file or the values so they can be added with a source.

flags.item: Automated product, price and review data needs Creators API access, which needs qualifying sales
flags.detail: The Creators API prerequisites require enrolment and 'at least 10 qualifying sales within the past 30 days' (PF-16, S04). Price and availability may be shown only if the link serves them or they come from the API (PF-04). Reviews and star ratings may be shown only through the API (PF-05). Pulling this data from amazon.com pages instead would not meet these rules, so it was not done.
flags.action: Confirm Associates enrolment status. Once eligible, register for the Creators API (S04) and provide credentials through a secure secret store, never in the repo.

flags.detail: The required statement (PF-01) is on every page. The FTC asks that a disclosure be hard to miss and placed with the endorsement (PF-20). The footer may not meet that standard for a product recommendation. Account enrolment could not be checked from this session.

flags.detail: The Associates Operating Agreement and Program Policies show a footer of '© 1996-2025'. The Amazon product pages show '© 1996-2026'. Both were read on 2026-11-13. The header dates (S01: October 15, 2025; S02: April 14, 2026) were used as the versions read.

flags.item: The AI analysis layer cannot use Creators API data without written approval
flags.detail: Creators API terms bar aggregating, analysing or repurposing Product Advertising Content without express prior written approval, and bar using Program Content to develop or train machine learning or language models (PF-23, PF-24, PF-25). The brief asks for an AI-powered platform. Any AI analysis of Amazon data is therefore blocked until approval is obtained. No AI analysis of Amazon data has been built.
flags.action: Owner: request written approval from Amazon for the planned analysis before building it, or limit the analysis to data the site already displays.

The disclosure text used on the site is the Associates wording (PF-01), which is verified; the FTC points are not used as a finding.
flags.action: Read the 2023 Endorsement Guides on ftc.gov before publishing marketing copy.

flags.item: Automation needs rules that have not been built: caching, price date stamps, disclaimers, agent identification, no scraping
flags.detail: The Creators API terms limit caching (PF-26), require a date and time stamp next to price or availability (PF-27), require a disclaimer (PF-28), cap call rates and file sizes (PF-29), require agents to identify themselves (PF-31), and forbid data mining and robots (PF-22). Program Content may be used only for Amazon products (PF-32), and click generation and price tracking are prohibited (PF-33, PF-34). None of this automation has been built.
flags.action: Design the data layer around these rules before any automation is built.

flags.item: Kitchen reference rate 4.50% is verified, but the listings' category is not
flags.detail: Amazon's Standard Commission Table 1 lists 'Kitchen' at 4.50% (S25; PF-38). The Onsite Table A lists 'Kitchen' at 1.25% for Onsite Content only (S26; PF-39). Neither is a product rate. To know which row applies, the category of each listing is needed. The product category is not stated in the text of the listings read (they show 'Home & Kitchen' as the department). The rate is therefore shown as a reference only and not on any product row. Raised by session 66a80e53 (PR #3). Update 2026-11-14: the category breadcrumb is now observed on each product page (Home & Kitchen > Kitchen & Dining > Small Appliances > Fryers > Air Fryers; S30-S32). Whether the commission schedule's 'Kitchen' category maps to this node is still not documented in any public source, so the reference rate stays a reference only.
flags.action: Owner: confirm each listing's category in Associates Central (or via the Creators API, once approved) before using any rate.

flags.item: Product identity rests on observed short-link redirects, not on documented identifiers
flags.detail: The three submitted codes are 9 characters and are not ASINs (FLG-001). Each submitted link resolves to exactly one Amazon listing, and the mapping was identical across 4 observations on 2026-11-13 and 2026-11-14 (S11-S13, S30-S32). Control tests on the shortener (recorded in COORDINATION.md, Z-V10 to Z-V14) show the codes are registered short codes: junk codes of the same length are rejected with 403/404. No official Amazon source documents the code-to-listing registry, so the association is recorded as observed, and this site treats each listing as the product its submitted link opens. If the owner intended different products, the tables must be re-pointed.
flags.action: Owner: confirm that the three listings recorded here are the intended products.

flags.item: Observed prices and star ratings are shown for analysis only; display on a live Associates site is restricted
flags.detail: Participation Requirements 2(b) (PF-04) allow a site to show prices and availability only when Amazon serves the link or through the Product Advertising API, and 6(t) (PF-05) bars displaying customer reviews or star ratings unless obtained through the API or a qualifying link. The prices and ratings on this site are dated observations (2026-11-14, S33-S35) kept for analysis, with a date stamp adjacent per PF-27. Before this site is used commercially, remove these values or re-source them via Special Links or the Creators API. Prices are also volatile deal prices (Z-F5 in COORDINATION.md).
flags.action: Remove or re-source observed prices/ratings via API or Special Links before commercial use.
